children: By Purvi Agarwal and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Wall Street was set for a higher open on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved appetite for the AI trade, while Netflix slipped after its forecast failed to impress investors.
Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm
rose 9.2% in premarket trading after he said on Tuesday that a merger of SpaceX and Tesla
would be "a good idea". SpaceX also posted its first profit as a public company. Tesla shares were up 1.5%.
Super Micro
jumped 12.7% after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient.
Peers HPE
and Dell
rose 4.8% and 7%, respectively.
Investors drew comfort from the reports as concerns over the profitability of the AI buildout triggered a selloff in AI-linked stocks last week, with data center operator CoreWeave
at the center of the storm. It was up 3.3% before the bell on Wednesday.

"At this stage, it's important to focus on what impacts the bottom line. Corporate earnings matter. Inflation matters because it influences what the Fed may do next," said Adam Sarhan, director at MarketTerminal.com.

"If the economy continues to grow without major headwinds, that supports higher earnings. In that environment, a lack of bad news becomes good news because it improves the outlook for corporate profits."
On the other hand, Netflix
dropped over 6.7% after the streaming giant issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for its fourth-quarter profit, days after laying off 6% of its workforce.
Investors are scrutinizing corporate earnings, especially from AI-aligned companies, for clues on whether the AI spending cycle is sustainable and the impact from rising oil prices.
Meta
and Tesla are scheduled to report after markets close.
At 8:44 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 159 points, or 0.3%, S&P 500 E-minis (EScv1) were up 20.25 points, or 0.26%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis
were up 167 points, or 0.56%.
Most chipmakers rose, with Nvidia
up 1.7%, Intel
gaining 2.2% and Advanced Micro Devices
adding 2%.
Semiconductors have had a volatile month so far, with the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index
marking eight consecutive sessions of declines, its longest losing streak in 18 years.
Amid the volatility, investors have flocked to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples, helping the Dow outshine the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq. The blue-chip index
has been trading at over one-month highs.
Meanwhile, oil prices remained elevated, with Brent crude futures
trading near $110 a barrel.
Data last week confirmed that price pressures were seeping into the US economy, and had broadened beyond energy products, supporting the case for another interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve.
However, markets expect the central bank to remain on hold ahead of the midterm elections on November 3.
Among others, AT&T
fell about 5% despite beating third-quarter revenue and profit estimates.
Elevance Health
rose around 1.1% after the health insurer lifted its 2026 profit forecast.
Futures up: Dow 0.30%, S&P 0.26%, Nasdaq 0.56%
